decisions.reason: The name, professional context, and all listed denials are supported by the source.
The role, dates, project work, training, and handbook are supported, but the claim that the end date was “corrected” is not: the source gives a date without describing any correction.

The project details and other claims are supported. However, the action “Worked through an example beside a supervisor” turns “I would sit beside a supervisor and work through an example” into a definite completed action; the source wording leaves that status ambiguous.
The source explicitly says Ada personally built Roster Note at Harbor Tools and identifies it as a separate SQL handover checklist.
The source supports training 12 coworkers in two workshops, writing a plain-language handbook, and including five worked examples.
The source supports the 5-to-2-hour weekly reconciliation result over six runs, the three-hour reduction, its team attribution, and Ada’s parser-and-checks contribution.
The source supports using Python for Dispatch Loom and personally writing its Python parser.
The source supports writing SQL checks for Dispatch Loom and personally building the separate SQL handover checklist.
The source explicitly says PostgreSQL was used for the production database.
The source explicitly says Git was used for version control.

Training dispatch coworkers is supported. The additional claim that Ada “worked through” a workflow example converts “I would ... work through an example” into a definite completed action, which the wording leaves ambiguous.
The degree, field, institution, and dates match the source.
